title: Rectangular prism
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop which consists of six lines. The first line starts at the origin (zero, zero) and extends to (zero point zero two eight three, zero). The second line moves from (zero point zero two eight three, zero) to (zero point zero two eight three, zero point zero two eight three). The third line goes from (zero point zero two eight three, zero point zero two eight three) to (zero point zero two six six, zero point zero two eight three). The fourth line travels from (zero point zero two six six, zero point zero two eight three) to (zero point zero two six six, zero point zero zero one seven). The fifth line runs from (zero point zero two six six, zero point zero zero one seven) to (zero, zero point zero zero one seven). Finally, the sixth line returns from (zero, zero point zero zero one seven) to the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero two eight three. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles as the coordinate system and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch by zero point seven five units along the normal direction to create the three-dimensional model. The final dimensions of the rectangular prism with rounded edges are zero point zero two eight three units in length, zero point zero two eight three units in width, and zero point seven five units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0283, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0283, 0.0283) \
     .lineTo(0.0266, 0.0283) \
     .lineTo(0.0266, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0017) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

# Display the model

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-shaped angle profile extruded along X
# Profile lies in the YZ plane: horizontal leg along Y, vertical leg along Z
L = 0.7500   # length along X
leg = 0.0283 # leg length
t = 0.0060   # wall thickness

profile = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0.0, 0.0)
    .lineTo(leg, 0.0)
    .lineTo(leg, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, leg)
    .lineTo(0.0, leg)
    .close()
)

r = profile.extrude(L)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

L = 0.7500
leg = 0.0283
t = 0.0030

horizontal = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(L, leg, t, centered=(True, False, False))
    .translate((L / 2, 0, 0))
)

vertical = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .box(L, t, leg, centered=(True, False, False))
    .translate((L / 2, leg - t, 0))
)

r = horizontal.union(vertical)
